peer_results.rationale: BAC candidates focus on general other income decreases, tax credit partnership losses, Visa litigation charges, and BSBY cessation charges. None specifically address impairment losses on equity investments or the specific comparative nature of impairment events in prior versus current years as described in the JPM target.

Citigroup candidates focus on credit provisions, net credit losses on loans, and overall net income drivers. These relate to credit risk and loan portfolios, not the equity investment impairments and valuation adjustments central to the JPM target topic.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, Asset & Wealth Management reported net revenues of $16.14 billion, a 16% increase driven by higher Equity investment gains and Management fees, while Private banking and lending increased and Debt investments decreased. Operating expenses were $11.83 billion, down 9% due to lower commercial real estate CIE impairments, resulting in pre-tax earnings of $4.55 billion, a significant increase from $1.36 billion in 2023, with pre-tax margins reaching 28%.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and GS discuss impairment losses and valuation adjustments impacting their respective investment portfolios in the current versus prior year comparison. JPM explicitly notes impairment losses on certain equity investments for both periods. GS discusses the composition of its Asset & Wealth Management revenues, noting that the prior year included net losses in real estate investments (an impairment/valuation event) which positively impacted the current year's growth by comparison, and also highlights a significant reduction in current-year expenses related to commercial real estate CIE impairments. While JPM focuses on the persistence of equity investment impairments, GS highlights the reversal or lower impact of real estate investment losses in the prior year and current year expense reductions from CRE impairments.

sentences.text: Both periods included impairment losses related to certain equity investments.
The increase in Management and other fees primarily reflected the impact of higher average assets under supervision.

Operating expenses were $11.83 billion for 2024, 9% lower than 2023, due to significantly lower expenses, including impairments, related to commercial real estate in CIEs, partially offset by higher compensation and benefits expenses (reflecting improved operating performance).
